chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz, from Ayyub ibn Nuh and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Hariz, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from his father who said:

I was in the mosque when Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) entered, and I did not recognize him. He had on a black turban with both its ends hanging between his shoulders. So I asked a man sitting near me, 'Who is this elder?' He said, 'What is the matter with you — you have not asked me about anyone who entered the mosque except this elder?' I said to him, 'I have not seen anyone enter the mosque with a finer appearance in my eyes than this elder, which is why I asked you about him.' He said, 'He is Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

So I arose, and the man and others arose; we gathered around him and greeted him. The man said to him, 'What is your view — may God keep you well — regarding a man who named a specific woman and said: on the day I marry her, she is divorced three times — then he later changes his mind and wants to marry her; is that permissible for him?' So he said: 'Divorce is only after marriage.'

Abdullah (son of the narrator) said: I and my father then went to Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), and my father narrated this hadith to him. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You are bearing witness upon Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) with this hadith?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.إِنَّمَا الطَّلَاقُ بَعْدَ النِّكَاحِ: Divorce is only after marriage — a foundational legal maxim of Islamic family law
key_terms.طَالِقٌ ثَلَاثاً: Triple divorce — pronouncing three divorces at once

ai.seo_question: Does a divorce pronounced before marriage take effect in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith is a biographical-legal narration in which Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (AS) is encountered in a mosque wearing a black turban and his distinguished appearance attracts attention, leading to a jurisprudential question about pre-nuptial divorce pronouncements. The Imam's ruling — 'divorce is only after marriage' — establishes a foundational principle of Islamic family law: a divorce pronounced before the marriage contract is concluded has no legal effect. This ruling is then corroborated by Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) who confirms the hadith's attribution to his great-grandfather.
